questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
In no particular order:
1) The opportunity to choose courses matching my interests.
2) A renowned university.
3) A country where I had the opportunity to experience a lot of things outside the campus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. ETH informs you, via email, every detail you need to know upon arrival - from signing up for courses to applying for a residence permit.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: See the previous question.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Via ETH, I signed up for WOKO housing - a student housing cooperative in Switzerland - where I was allocated a room in the dorm of Alte Landstrasse, Zollikon.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living off campus in one of the WOKO dorms is a great opportunity to meet other exchange students from around the world - and to make new friends.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: WOKO does not have enough accomodation to host every incomming exchange student. Hence, one is not guaranteed a place in one of their dorms. I therefore recommend to search for other housing opportunities as a plan B.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: ETH informs you about everything you need to know about the course registration process.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You sign up for courses online in a similar way to how you do at UCPH. For some courses, you have to get permission from the professor. However, this is easy to obtain by simply writing them an email.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Informative emails, online meetings by ETH, help from ETH's student administration.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got every course I signed up for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start your course registration process early. There are a lot of courses to choose from, which can make the registration process quite long.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the courses is generally high. Having a found mathematical background helps a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Lectures are held in pretty much the same way. The TA sessions are, however, thaught in a different way. Usually, it is one TA teaching the whole class in only some of the problems.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
i) German intensive course B1
ii) Numerical solutions of stochastic ordinary differential equations
iii) Statistical modelling
iv) Machine learning in finance and insurance
v) Seminar in computational finance
vi) Asset management: advanced investments (A University of Zürich course)
vii) Data visualisation in finance (A University of Zürich course)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Numerical solutions of stochastic ordinary differential equations. 
A great course for learning how to carry out simulations and mathematical convergence analysis for stochastic models originating from applications such as mathematical finance. However, one should note that the workload of this course is very high, and the home assignments are difficult. 

Statistical modelling. 
After finishing this course my understanding of statistical models - linear models, non-parametric model, general linear models, etc. - has deepened a lot. In short: a good course to take if you want a solid mathematical and intuitive understanding of statistical models.

Machine learning in finance and insurance. 
A good introduction to machine learning (ML). The lectures are theoretically orientated, ensuring you get a solid understanding of the field. On the other hand, the projects are finance/insurance orientated, showing how ML can be used in these fields.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Attending ETH, you can sign up for an ASVZ membership for free. This is an organisation offering classes on +50 different sports. Moreover, you can workout in their gyms for free.
The biggest ball party in Europe: Polyball.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Go on hikes across Switzerland
Attend ERASMUS events.
Travel to France, Italy, or another nearby country.
Attend parties at the dorm of Meierwiesenstrasse.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on hikes - Switzerland is full of beautiful hiking trails.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Switzerland is very similar to Denmark in terms of culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find any culture differences challenging.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Nothing to add.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Courses are in general smaller than 7.5 ECTS, but the workload of a single course can easily feel like a +7.5 ECTS course. A very high workload should therefore be expected.
2) Priorize social events.
3) Plan out your semester.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing to add.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I have met and all the experiences I have added to my scrapbook. Additionally, the knowledge I have gained through my courses.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing my social life and my studies.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
